app/package.json:21 — exact-pinned RC version (no caret), so builds can't silently pick up a newer RC

containment.rationale: The RC surface is confined to one config file, one pinned devDependency, and the start script; swapping the server runtime would touch three lines total, and no source file would change.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:4-7 — plugin stack (tanstackStart, nitro, viteReact) is byte-for-byte the framework's official current example (TanStack/router examples/react/start-basic/vite.config.ts uses the same three plugins)
app/package.json:5-8 — build/start scripts match the official example's 'vite build' / 'node .output/server/index.mjs', satisfying the SPEC's production-serve requirement
app/src/routes/index.tsx:26-33 — loaderDeps + validateSearch: stable, purpose-built router APIs instead of newer experimental search-param utilities
justification.rationale: The single non-stable dependency is not a choice the app made gratuitously — it is the documented and only current way to build/serve TanStack Start v1.169 (the framework dropped its bundled server), and it buys exactly what the SPEC requires: a production server behind npm start. Everything else is stable API.

findings.issue: Production server runtime is nitro 3.0.261029-rc, a release candidate; nitro v3 has no stable release (npm dist-tag latest is an RC) and nitro's own README still calls v2 the current stable line.
findings.suggestion: This follows official TanStack Start guidance, so keep it, but treat RC bumps as breaking-change candidates: keep the exact pin (already done, no caret), note the RC in the README, and re-verify the build on every nitro upgrade.

findings.issue: The start script hard-codes nitro's output layout ('.output/server/index.mjs'), so a nitro major change or a switch to another Start hosting target (e.g. node-server) breaks start silently.
findings.suggestion: Add a comment or a smoke check that the built file exists before start; if TanStack Start later ships a target-agnostic start command, switch to it.

summary: The app is deliberately conservative: every line of source uses long-stable TanStack Router/Start APIs with no unstable_ or experimental_ names. The single non-stable piece is the nitro v3 RC server runtime, which is confined to vite.config.ts, one exactly-pinned devDependency, and the start script — and it is the officially documented integration for the framework version the app targets. Risk is real but small: nitro v3 has never cut a stable release, so upgrades need deliberate review.
